where: Results, Cupiennius salei (PMC full text; sentence read on two fetches)
quote: The initial pupil-to-lens ratio was found to be in the order of 0.5, i.e. only a fourth of the total projected lens surface is free from the pigment shield shortly after ecdysis.
note: new trait: pupil_lens_ratio (pupil diameter divided by lens diameter in the photographed eye; no key in BRIEF's table or check.py's TRAITS records pupil size; main also uses the unlisted keys pupil (free text) and pupil_area_ratio (pupil constriction range, a light response), and neither fits a post-moult aperture fraction; adopting the key is the owner's decision). Accepted name: World Spider Catalog (wsc.nmbe.ch/species/8003) Cupiennius salei (Keyserling, 1877), SPECIES ACCEPTED, family Trechaleidae (older papers place it in Ctenidae). Not on main (grep by species and DOI). Licence: PMC page states open access under the Creative Commons Attribution License; Crossref lists CC BY 4.0. Juveniles only (nine animals in three age groups of 5, 7 and 9 months, N = 4, 3 and 2); the sentence does not separate the posterior median (Table 1) from the anterior median (Table 2) eyes, whose absolute pupil diameters differ (the AM pupils were smaller at every stage). Measured from photographs of living, tethered, anaesthetised (CO2 or cooling) spiders in software (circle fitted to points placed by hand), reared in a greenhouse at 15-28 C, 70-80% relative humidity, 12 h:12 h day:night. The same paper photographed Lycosa tarentula (one animal) and Heteropoda venatoria (five animals) and reports pigment rings after ecdysis that nearly vanish in the following days, but gives no pupil diameters for them. Adult pupil size is not measured here. Diameter measurement uncertainty 5-10 µm.
